answer: Bonded deposits make sybil attacks costly: to join the agent economy, each identity must lock a refundable stake, like cargo held at a wharf before it can trade. If peers detect fake or duplicate behavior, the stake is slashed, so every forged identity risks real loss. Honest agents, by contrast, grow a shared meadow of verified interactions — a public history of useful work — that a newcomer cannot fake overnight. Even if an attacker plants many identities, each one must fund its own oasis of stake and survive scrutiny, turning a cheap flood of fakes into an expensive, slow trickle.
